loci.name: tac-current-magnitude-and-repricing-path
loci.one_line: What is Google TAC's CURRENT (not 2022) magnitude and margin, and what specific magnitude/timing of price compression follows from the court's non-exclusive annual-rebidding remedy?
loci.rationale: The only quantified TAC figure in the corpus is the court's ~$20B, explicitly a 2022 WORLDWIDE figure (source-analysis-us-v-google-remedies-opinion-doc-1436-sept-2-2025; united-states-district-court-3). A single analyst note gives a materially different, more current figure — Morgan Stanley's Erik Woodring estimates 'over $25 billion annually... at 95%-plus margins' (how-the-google-antitrust-ruling-reshapes-search-ai-and-more) — but it is unclear whether this is US-only or worldwide, and it is a single sell-side voice, not independently corroborated in the corpus. The contradiction graph's top-ranked cluster (tac-durability-toothless-vs-erosion) explicitly states both sides' experts (Chipty for plaintiffs, Murphy for Google) agree the price will compress under annual rebidding but 'no source quantifies' the magnitude or speed (scope_overlap field, cluster rank 1). This is the single most load-bearing unresolved number for the falsification test: the orchestrator's provisional sizing (TAC ~10.2% of total gross profit, ~24% of Services gross profit) rests on the stale 2022 figure, and the valuation consequence of the remedy hinges entirely on how fast and how far the rate falls after the six-year clock starts running (60 days after final judgment, per the remedies opinion).

loci.name: appstore-commission-magnitude-and-margin
loci.one_line: What is a defensible range for global and US App Store commission revenue, and what margin should convert that revenue to gross profit — using court-surfaced figures, not just one commercial estimator?
loci.rationale: Every commission-revenue figure in the corpus traces to a single commercial estimator, Appfigures: 'Apple earned >GBP7.6bn (~$10.1bn) from US App Store commissions in 2024... >GBP20.5bn (~$27.39bn) globally in 2024' (how-apple-makes-billions-from-the-app-storeand-why-90-of-sales-now-escape-its-co), restated by MacRumors (apples-us-app-store-commission-revenue-down-18-this-year-macrumors) and BigGo (apple-makes-rare-admission-of-regulatory-hit-as-app-store-commission-model-erode) — the redundancy audit itself flags this as 'two commercial estimators... restated across many outlets' with 'management's oral admission the only independent confirmation of DIRECTION; no filing quantifies it.' On margin, the only court language in the corpus is qualitative — the 30% commission 'allowed [Apple] to reap supracompetitive operating margins' (epic-games-wins-injunction-against-apple-pdf-legal-remedy-injunction) — with no percentage attached. The orchestrator's own falsification-test sizing explicitly flags '~90% margin on commissions is my assumption, not evidence' as one of three numbers that 'carry the whole thesis and each needs a defended range.' The 2021 Epic v. Apple trial produced extensive court-surfaced App Store segment financial data (Apple's own internal reporting, expert testimony) that is NOT present anywhere in this corpus — a primary-source gap directly on point given the domain notes' instruction that court records outrank estimates.

loci.name: ai-late-follower-chosen-vs-revealed
loci.one_line: Is Apple's late-follower AI posture a chosen capital-allocation advantage (rent capability as inference commoditises) or a revealed execution failure the company is now managing well after the fact?
loci.rationale: This is the contradiction graph's own top dialectical candidate (cluster ai-late-follower-chosen-vs-revealed, rank 4, decision_relevance high), and it maps directly onto the query's mandated reader-prior test #1. The corpus contains a first-party admission that cuts against the 'chosen' framing: Craig Federighi stated the March 2025 Siri delay was caused by the V1 architecture failing to meet the quality bar, 'not a strategic choice' (apples-siri-revamp-reportedly-delayed-again-techcrunch), against ~18 months of repeated slippage (apple-reportedly-targets-spring-2026-for-launch-of-delayed-ai-siri-upgrade-but-i) and a cumulative 2020-2025 AI spend gap of ~$20B vs $141-205B for the hyperscalers (725b-on-ai-where-big-tech-is-spending-in-2026). Set against this: capex fell 19-28% YoY every FY2026 quarter while R&D rose 32-34%, explicitly tied to AI (aapl-20260627, aapl-20260328, aapl-20251227), a falling inference-cost curve (llm-inference-prices-have-fallen-rapidly-but-unequally-across-tasks-epoch-ai), and a market that rewarded Apple's restraint during the Feb 2026 hyperscaler capex selloff (660b-capex-bill-triggers-900b-wipeout-why-apple-shares-outperform-amazon-and-goo). The orchestrator's own synthesis calls this 'the strongest candidate for a dialectical locus' and proposes a split verdict (origin revealed, current management capital-efficient) — but that verdict was reached without depth investigation and needs testing against what has actually happened since (iOS 27 Siri launch reception, any post-Q3-FY26 capex/R&D data, and whether the market read of the Feb 2026 selloff holds up).

opposing_positions.position: Chosen: deliberate capital discipline, renting capability (Gemini-powered Siri, ~$1B/yr) as inference costs collapse; capex fell 19-28% YoY every FY2026 quarter even as R&D rose ~33%, and markets rewarded the restraint when hyperscalers lost ~$900B in a week over AI capex ROI concerns.

Revealed: Federighi stated on the record the Siri delay was a failure to meet Apple's own quality bar, 'not a strategic choice'; the overhaul has slipped ~18 months across three announced dates, and Apple's cumulative 2020-2025 AI spend (~$20B) trails every hyperscaler by an order of magnitude in a pattern predating any 'wait for commoditisation' rationale.

loci.rationale: The query explicitly names the EU DMA as the natural experiment for testing whether lock-in is structural or regulation-removable (research question 6). The orchestrator notes flag, twice, an 'AUDITED ABSENCE confirmed: no EU/DMA phone-level switching data exists' and that 'the natural experiment the brief relies on tests only the weak form.' loci.rationale: Research question 7 and one of the four mandated 'minimum necessary components' require this calculation explicitly, and it is listed as only 'adequate' (not well-covered) in coverage-gaps.md, with no defended computation surfaced yet. The orchestrator's own notes flag a 'MAJOR REVERSAL': nine-month FY2026 Products revenue grew +16.9% vs Services +14.1% (aapl-8k-q1fy2026, aapl-8k-q2fy2026, aapl-8k-q3fy2026, aapl-20260627), meaning 'hardware maturity' — the premise research question 7 is built on — does not currently hold, even though the replacement cycle has structurally lengthened (2.9y to 3.8y, iphone-statistics-2026-revenue-market-share-and-the-replacement-cycle-axis-intel).
